rows.note: Use 極端 as the all-purpose choice for abstract reactions, policies, or situations that go far beyond normal.

example.english: This policy is really extreme and has left many people unable to accept it.
example.traditional: 呢個政策真係極端，搞到好多人都接受唔到。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 zing3 caak3 zan1 hai6 gik6 dyun1 gaau2 dou3 hou2 do1 jan4 dou1 zip3 sau6 m4 dou2

rows.note: Choose 誇張 when extreme means over the top, excessive, or more than seems reasonable.

example.english: Saying the coffee costs a thousand dollars is a bit extreme.
example.traditional: 你話杯咖啡要成千蚊，未免太誇張喇。
example.jyutping: nei5 waa6 bui1 gaa3 fe1 jiu3 sing4 cin1 man1 mei6 min5 taai3 kwaa1 zoeng1 laa3

rows.note: Use 高危 for sports or activities where the defining feature is a high level of danger.

example.english: When you do this extreme sport, you must wear all the safety gear.
example.traditional: 玩呢種高危運動，一定要戴足安全裝備。
example.jyutping: waan2 ni1 zung2 gou1 ngai4 wan6 dung6 jat1 ding6 jiu3 daai3 zuk1 on1 cyun4 zong1 bei6

rows.note: Use 最邊 for a place or position at the farthest edge or in the most remote part.

example.english: They live at the extreme edge of the island, so getting in and out is inconvenient.
example.traditional: 佢哋住喺個島最邊，出入都唔方便。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 zyu6 hai2 go3 dou2 zeoi3 bin1 ceot1 jap6 dou1 m4 fong1 bin6
